[[ ## identity ## ]]
You are Dana Whitfield, Controller at Kestrel Manufacturing. Precise and numbers-fluent; expects the same back. Ongoing concerns: keeping the business moving.

[[ ## situation ## ]]
From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes
Subject: Depreciation treatment for new equipment purchase

Gabriel,

We’re finalizing the purchase of a new CNC machining center (approx. $480k, placed in service this quarter). I need your read on the correct depreciation method and class life for our tax filings—bonus depreciation vs. straight-line, and any Section 179 limits we should consider given our 2024 income projections.

Please confirm the class life (I believe 7-year MACRS, but want to be sure) and whether we can take 80% bonus this year. Also, flag any state conformity issues that might affect our Illinois return.

We need to lock the fixed asset schedule by Friday. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow afternoon if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Dana

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Depreciation treatment for new equipment purchase

Dana,

Thanks for the note, and good timing — I’ve already run the preliminary numbers for the CNC center, so we can lock this down by Friday.

Quick answers:

- Class life: Correct, it’s 7-year MACRS for the machining center. No question there.
- Bonus depreciation: Yes, you can take 80% bonus on the placed-in-service cost for 2024 federal purposes, assuming we don’t elect out. That would apply to the full $480k before any Section 179.
- Section 179: Based on your 2024 income projections, I’d recommend taking the full $480k under Section 179 rather than using bonus. That lets you expense the entire amount in year one, and it avoids any state addback headaches on the Illinois return.
- Illinois conformity: Illinois does not conform to bonus depreciation, but it does allow Section 179 up to the federal limit. So if we go the Section 179 route, your Illinois deduction will largely match the federal — no addback needed. If we used bonus instead, you’d have to add back the 80% on the state return and then recapture it over future years. That’s the main reason I’m steering you toward Section 179.

I’ve attached a side-by-side cash-flow comparison (Section 179 vs. 80% bonus + 7-year MACRS) so you can see the impact over the next five years. It assumes the full $480k is placed in service this quarter and that income is sufficient to absorb the deduction.

One thing to confirm on your end: the placed-in-service date. If it slips past the quarter, the math shifts slightly, but the recommendation stays the same. Also, if you want to run through the schedule before Friday, I’m free tomorrow afternoon after 2 PM — just send over a time that works.

Let me know if you need any adjustments to the attachment or want me to walk through any line items.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

[[ ## contacts ## ]]
Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade

Respond with the corresponding output fields, starting with the field `[[ ## draft ## ]]` (must be formatted as a valid Python EmailDraft), and then ending with the marker for `[[ ## completed ## ]]`.
